Title: 5 arrested, others sought over viral Pudu nightclub brawl
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Five men with records for violent and drug-related offences have been arrested over a brawl outside a nightclub in Pudu, with police hunting for other suspects still at large.
Wangsa Maju district police chief assistant commissioner Annas Sulaiman said the men, aged between 19 and 30, were believed to have been directly involved in the incident outside the nightclub.
"Preliminary investigations found that the fight stemmed from a misunderstanding between several individuals before escalating into a larger brawl outside the club.
"Police also seized a black Perodua Myvi believed to have been used during the incident," he said in a statement today.
The incident, which was uploaded on Facebook, showed a Perodua Myvi ramming into a parked car before several people were seen fighting outside the premises.
Annas said all suspects had been remanded for five days from Monday until Friday to assist in investigations.
"The case is being investigated under Section 307 of the Penal Code for attempted murder, Section 148 for possessing weapons during a riot and Section 427 for mischief," he said.
Those convicted under Section 307 could face up to 10 years in jail and a fine.
Those with information on the incident can contact investigating officer Insp Jeychandran Velayudan at 03-9289 9222 or 010-214 6297, the Kuala Lumpur police hotline at 03-2115 9999, or any nearby police station.

Title: Teenager dies after touching lamp post in Bestari Jaya
Article:
SHAH ALAM: A 15-year-old boy died after being electrocuted while touching a lamp post at a residential park in Taman Pancaran, Bestari Jaya, yesterday.
Kuala Selangor police chief Superintendent Azaharudin Tajuddin said police received a call about the incident at 10.32pm.
"The Kuala Selangor District Police Headquarters Operations Room received a call regarding a boy who was found unconscious and believed to be dead.
"Investigations found that the victim was reportedly taking a break while playing futsal at the residential area park before touching the lamp post and collapsing," he said in a statement today.
Azaharudin said an examination of the victim's body found no criminal elements and the case was being investigated as a sudden death report (SDR).
"The teenager was confirmed dead at the scene by Health Ministry personnel. A post-mortem was conducted, and the cause of death was found to be 'consistent with electrocution'," he said.
He urged anyone with information about the incident to contact the Operations Room at 03-32891222 or the nearest police station.

Title: 4 arrested for allegedly robbing foreigners in Kodiang
Article:
JITRA: Police have arrested four men believed to be involved in armed gang robberies targeting homes occupied by foreigners in the Kodiang area of Kedah.
Kubang Pasu district police chief superintendent Mohd Radzi Abdul Rahim said the case came to light after a 28-year-old Myanmar national lodged a police report on Aug 17, claiming that his rented house in Kampung Kodiang Lama had been broken into by three masked men.
He said that in the incident at about 1.30am, the three suspects, dressed in dark clothing and wearing gloves, knocked on the door before assaulting and threatening the victim with what was believed to be a knife.
"The suspects also pointed a knife at the victim's body and neck before ordering him to hand over his valuables," he said at a press conference today.
He said the items handed over by the victim included two necklaces, a ring, a pendant, a pair of earrings, two mobile phones and a wallet containing a UNHCR card.
The victim suffered injuries to his hands and right leg, as well as a wound to his abdomen, he said.
He said police subsequently arrested four suspects aged between 22 and 37 at three locations, namely, Ipoh, Kodiang and Kangar.
Police also seized several items believed to be linked to the incident, including four mobile phones, a green-and-black zipped sling bag, two UNHCR cards, a pawnshop receipt, a folding knife and a small knife with a wooden handle and sheath.
"Further investigations found that all the suspects were believed to have targeted homes occupied by foreigners in the Kodiang area, particularly Myanmar nationals.
"They would go to the targeted homes wearing face coverings and armed with knives before carrying out the robberies."
Radzi said the case was being investigated under Sections 395/397 of the Penal Code for gang robbery with weapons.
All the suspects have been remanded until Sept 3 to assist in investigations.

Title: KLCI faces fresh selling pressure as foreign outflows persist
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The FBM KLCI is expected to remain in consolidation mode with a slight downward bias this week as investors contend with persistent external and domestic headwinds, while continued foreign selling weighs on sentiment.
Kenanga Research said market sentiment was likely to remain cautious as investors digested hawkish remarks by US Federal Reserve chairman Kevin Warsh.
Attention will now turn to Bank Negara Malaysia's Monetary Policy Committee meeting and the US August non-farm payrolls report.
The research house said the FBM KLCI fell 0.61 per cent, or 10.60 points week-on-week, to 1,725.88 points last week, as late-week profit-taking ahead of the extended Merdeka break outweighed earlier gains.
Sentiment was initially supported by firmer regional markets, a stronger ringgit and lower crude oil prices, which lifted selected banking and YTL-related heavyweights.
However, mixed corporate earnings and profit-taking weighed on sentiment towards the end of the week, resulting in broad-based selling on Friday.
Kenanga Research said the KLCI remained within its ascending channel and above its key weekly moving averages, keeping the broader uptrend intact, although near-term momentum had softened.
It identified support levels at 1,711 and 1,707 points, while resistance was seen at 1,735 and 1,753 points.
The cautious near-term outlook comes despite the KLCI having staged a strong recovery from its year-to-date low, with Hong Leong Investment Bank Research (HLIB Research) describing the recent weakness as a healthy consolidation.
HLIB Research said the KLCI had rallied 95 points from its year-to-date low of 1,655 points on June 29 to 1,753.20 points on Aug 26.
The medium-term uptrend remained intact, with the index holding above its 50-day, 100-day and 200-day moving averages at 1,711, 1,710 and 1,698 points, respectively.
However, it said the index was likely to remain range-bound amid heightened Middle East tensions, the conclusion of the August corporate results season and continued foreign outflows.
HLIB Research said a decisive breakout above 1,734 points could signal renewed upside towards 1,753, 1,766 and the year-to-date high of 1,771 points, while a break below the 1,698-1,710-point range could heighten downside risk towards 1,685 points.
The continued foreign selling cited by HLIB Research was reflected in the latest fund flow data, with MBSB Investment Bank Bhd reporting that foreign institutions extended their net selling streak on Bursa Malaysia to four consecutive weeks, recording RM366.0 million in net outflows last week.
In its weekly fund flow report for the week ended August 28, MBSB IB said local institutions, meanwhile, extended their net buying streak to five consecutive weeks with RM200.5 million in net inflows, while retailers returned to net buying with RM165.5 million in net inflows.
It said foreign selling was concentrated in financial services, construction and telecommunications and media, which recorded net outflows of RM245.5 million, RM92.4 million and RM86.3 million, respectively.
Against this backdrop, RHB Research said the weakness was also evident in the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI futures contract (FKLI), which is based on the FBM KLCI.
It said the FKLI fell 23 points to close at 1,700 points last Friday after hitting an intraday high of 1,732 points and a low of 1,693.50 points, with its technical setup weakening after breaching its 50-day simple moving average.
RHB Research said continued selling pressure could pull the FKLI towards 1,680 points, although it expected bulls to defend that support level.
A recovery above the 50-day simple moving average (SMA), it said, would signal a resumption of the upward trend.

Title: Missing Malaysian declared dead 2 years after swept away in India
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court in Penang today declared Dr Balraj Sethi, who went missing after being swept away by strong currents in a river in India 2 years ago, dead.
Balraj, who was then Novartis Malaysia's medical affairs head, disappeared in September 2024 after jumping into the Alaknanda River in an attempt to rescue his father, K. Suresh Chandra.
Suresh, who survived after being rescued by workers nearby, subsequently filed an application seeking a declaration of Balraj's death.
According to the court's notes of proceedings, the court found that Suresh had established, on the balance of probabilities, that Balraj died on Sept 24, 2024, after considering the originating summons, supporting affidavit, written submissions and documentary evidence.
The court also allowed Suresh to submit the court order to the Registrar for the registration of Balraj's death and the issuance of a presumed death certificate.
No order was made as to costs.
Suresh was represented by lawyer Nishantel Kaur.
The matter was heard before Muhammad Firdaus Abdul Wahab.
Balraj, 40, had travelled to India on Sept 14, 2024, with his parents, son and cousin for a 10-day pilgrimage.
The family had visited three shrines before arriving at Badrinath Temple on Sept 24 to complete their pilgrimage.
His father, then 67, had gone near the river to perform tarpan, a ritual in which water is offered to ancestors, when he was swept away by strong currents.
Balraj jumped into the river in an attempt to save him but was also carried away.
Workers nearby managed to rescue Suresh about 200m from the spot, but Balraj could not be found despite a search and rescue operation.

Title: Between Us: Gen Z meets Gen Merdeka [WATCH]
Article:
MERDEKA may have just been celebrated, but the history, memories and meaning behind Aug 31 continue to resonate across generations.
That was the premise behind NST Between Us: Gen Z v Gen Merdeka, which brought together three young Malaysians and two veterans who were teenagers when Malaya achieved independence in 1957.
They were Lt Col (Rtd) Datuk Zarazilah Mohamed Ali, 86; former Special Branch officer Datuk Paul Kiong, 82; Petaling Jaya councillor Loh Y Lun, 26; researcher Graciely Stefanie O'Hara, 26; and gap-year student Rajdev Sachdev Singh, 20.
[[nid:1523572]]
The session began with a light-hearted Merdeka trivia challenge before moving into personal memories of growing up in the years surrounding independence.
The veterans recalled a Malaysia shaped by the Malayan Emergency and communist insurgency, as well as a strong sense of patriotism among young people who wanted to contribute to the country.
They also remembered a more carefree time, when neighbours' doors were open and friendships were formed across racial and religious lines without much thought given to differences.
[[nid:1523571]]
For the Gen Z participants, those memories prompted questions about whether Malaysians today still share the same sense of togetherness.
Technology became another point of discussion, with the veterans reflecting on a time before mobile phones and instant messaging, while the younger generation offered a counterpoint that technology can also connect people.
The discussion ultimately moved beyond nostalgia and history to the meaning of patriotism today.
Watch the full discussion on NST Online's YouTube channel and revisit our Merdeka series to relive the moments, memories and stories that shaped Malaysia.

Title: Malaysia's resilience boosts appeal of government bonds
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's stable outlook and resilient fundamentals are expected to support foreign demand for government bonds, Malaysian Government Securities (MGS), MARC Ratings said.
In a statement, the rating agency said rising sovereign risks in the region could further enhance the country's appeal among investors.
This comes amid sovereign credit outlook downgrades for Indonesia and the Philippines in the first half of 2026.
Foreign bond flows into Malaysia, however, reversed to a net outflow of RM5.6 billion in July from a RM4.9 billion inflow in June, while foreign holdings of MGS declined to 20.1 per cent of the market from 20.6 per cent.
MARC Ratings said the outflow was largely driven by higher US Treasury yields, which increased the relative appeal of US government bonds.
In contrast, foreign equity flows turned positive at RM200 million in July from a RM2.5 billion outflow in June, supported by stronger domestic growth prospects.
Malaysia's improving external position could also strengthen investor confidence.
Exports jumped 38 per cent year-on-year in July to a record RM193.6 billion, led by electrical and electronic (E&E) products amid the global artificial intelligence investment cycle.
Strong machinery, petroleum and liquefied natural gas (LNG) exports also contributed to the expansion.
Continued disruptions to Middle Eastern energy supplies could further support Malaysia's LNG exports as global buyers diversify supply sources, while firm US demand for E&E products is expected to sustain external momentum.
The ringgit strengthened to around RM4.04 against the US dollar as of Aug 24, from RM4.09 at the end of July, supported by the strong external trade position.
"While a stronger US dollar and higher-for-longer US Treasury yields may continue to cap ringgit upside, resilient macroeconomic fundamentals, robust exports and sustained foreign direct investment inflows should continue to provide support for the ringgit. We maintain our end-2026 ringgit forecast at 4.00–4.15 against the US dollar," it said.
Meanwhile, MGS yields rose by about four to 13 basis points across the curve as at Aug 24, reflecting spillovers from higher global bond yields and expectations that stronger domestic conditions give Bank Negara Malaysia greater scope to normalise its monetary policy.
MARC Ratings said the overnight policy rate (OPR) currently stands at 2.75 per cent and could gradually move towards three per cent over time.
The 10-year MGS yield forecast for end-2026 has therefore been revised upwards to 3.75-3.85 per cent from 3.60-3.70 per cent previously, with the 2027 forecast at 3.85-3.95 per cent.
"The revision reflects a hawkish repricing of Federal Reserve (Fed) expectations, with the recent Jackson Hole Economic Symposium reinforcing higher-for-longer policy rate expectations, alongside a firmer US dollar and scope for anticipated OPR normalisation," it added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Muhyiddin played golf at Tropicana on July 19, 2020, court told
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A witness told the High Court today that former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin was at the Tropicana Golf & Country Resort to play golf on July 19, 2020.
Tropicana Golf & Country Resort Bhd (TGCRB) group head of security, S. Saravanan, 56, testified that a check on the Green Fee Tag showed Muhyiddin was among 15 players registered to play at the golf club that day.
"Based on my check of the Golf Registration System at TGCRB on July 19, 2020, there was an invoice registered under Muhyiddin's name. The invoice showed golf service fees amounting to RM0, as it was fully covered by the Golf Club (complimentary).
"Based on the Green Fee Tag, the players that day comprised four flights (groups) involving 15 players. They were Muhyiddin, Natan, Shahran, Syed Hafiz, Esa, Tony, Azman, Adlan, Faliq, Shahjuan, CDR Sharif, Noor Zilan, Adam, Rashid and Mr Jared Ethan Ang Tzer Shkn," he said.
The 28th prosecution witness said this when reading his witness statement during Muhyiddin's trial, in which he faces seven charges of abuse of power and money laundering involving the Jana Wibawa project.
Saravanan said that every player must be registered and have their name entered into the Green Fee Tag system for record-keeping and insurance purposes.
On Aug 27 last year, Bumiputera Contractors Association of Malaysia president Datuk Seri Azman Yusoff, 54,  told the court that he had met Muhyiddin at a golf tournament at the same club in July 2020, during which Muhyiddin briefed him on projects under the Jana Wibawa programme.
However, Azman's testimony regarding that meeting was challenged by lawyer Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad, who disputed that the meeting had taken place, and further claimed that the golf tournament in question took place in October rather than July.
Saravanan said he could not ascertain whether the game that day was a tournament or merely a friendly match, based on the number of players involved.
"Usually, if they are playing in a small group among themselves, we refer to it as a 'friendly' between those flights," he said.
"A tournament refers to a large group, usually more than 10 flights with over 40 players, and can involve up to 260 people," the witness said during examination-in-chief by deputy public prosecutor (DPP) Khairunnisa Hazwani Omar.
During the proceedings, DPP Noralis Mat informed the court that the prosecution would not be calling businessman Adam Radlan Adam Muhammad as a prosecution witness, but would likely offer him as a defence witness instead.
Muhyiddin, 79, who was then Prime Minister and Bersatu president, was charged with four counts of abuse of power for allegedly soliciting RM232.5 million in bribes for the political party from Bukhary Equity Sdn Bhd, Nepturis Sdn Bhd, Mamfor Sdn Bhd, and Datuk Azman Yusoff in connection with the Jana Wibawa project.
He was accused of committing the offence at the Prime Minister's Office, Bangunan Perdana Putra, Putrajaya between March 1, 2020, and Aug 20, 2021, under Section 23(1) of the MACC Act 2009, which carries a maximum penalty of 20 years' jail and a fine of five times the value of the gratification or RM10,000, whichever is higher, upon conviction.
The Pagoh MP also faces three charges of receiving RM200 million in unlawful proceeds from Bukhary Equity Sdn Bhd, which were deposited into Bersatu's Ambank and CIMB Bank accounts, allegedly committed in Petaling Jaya and Kuala Lumpur between February 2021 and July 2022.
These charges were brought under Section 4(1)(b) of the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001, which carries a maximum penalty of 15 years' jail and a fine of either five times the value of the proceeds from unlawful activities or RM5 million, whichever is higher.
The trial before Judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin resumes tomorrow.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Israel PM's wife shares conspiracy theory about opposition figure
Article:
JERUSALEM: Sara Netanyahu, the wife of the Israeli prime minister, has claimed an opposition figure was aware of the plan for Hamas's Oct 7, 2023 attack before it happened.
Her remarks, which triggered outrage across Israel's opposition, highlight the country's deep political polarisation ahead of close-fought elections to be held on Oct 27.
In a television interview broadcast on Monday evening, Sara Netanyahu lashed out at Yair Golan, the former deputy military chief of staff who heads Israel's centre-left Democrats party.
She suggested Golan was "already dressed and ready" at dawn on Oct 7, 2023, "while others knew nothing, including the prime minister."
Sara Netanyahu's interview was broadcast on Israel's Channel 14, which is close to the government. The comments triggered swift outrage from the opposition.
Golan's party said it strongly condemned the "vile and deceitful" remarks.
"Spreading conspiracies against Major General Yair Golan, and smearing his heroism on Oct 7, is crossing a red line that borders on insanity," it wrote on X.
Gadi Eisenkot, a former army chief who has emerged as the frontrunner to challenge Netanyahu, slammed the "mad conspiracy of betrayal" spread by the prime minister's wife.
In a post on X, he said the comments were "intended only to stoke hatred and perpetuate Netanyahu's rule."
Sara Netanyahu's accusations reflect recurrent conspiracy theories among a part of the Israeli political class.
According to a poll conducted for Channel 13 in August, 40 per cent of Israelis, and 63 per cent of voters for the current right-wing coalition, believe that internal treason led to the Oct 7 attack – the deadliest day in Israel's history.
Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving prime minister who has billed himself as the guarantor of the country's safety, has deflected blame for the attack, saying that security officials should have woken him from his sleep.
Hamas's attack on Israel resulted in the deaths of 1,221 people, according to an AFP tally based on official Israeli figures. Fighters also took 251 hostages – 44 of them already dead – into Gaza.
Israel responded with a massive offensive in Gaza that has killed at least 73,454 people, according to the Palestinian territory's health ministry, which operates under Hamas authority and whose figures are considered reliable by the United Nations.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Norway's new king to swear oath before parliament after Harald's death
Article:
OSLO:  King Haakon VIII of Norway will on Tuesday take an oath before parliament following the death of his father, pledging to uphold the Nordic country's constitution and laws in the latest in a series of ceremonies marking the passing of the crown.
Haakon's father King Harald died on Friday at the age of 89. Since then, tens of thousands of Norwegians have streamed to the royal palace to lay flowers, drawings, candles and flags.
Many have praised Harald's warmth and sense of inclusiveness, while Haakon described him as a wonderful father in his first address to the nation as sovereign.
The monarchy remains broadly popular: 72 per cent of Norwegians support it, while 20 per cent favour a republic or another form of government, according to a Norstat poll for broadcaster NRK published Tuesday, the first poll on the issue taken since Harald's death.
The previous Norstat poll, conducted in May, showed support for the monarchy at 64 per cent.
QUEEN METTE-MARIT TO ATTEND
The ceremony in the 169-seat chamber, which will start at 1100 GMT, will underline the foundations of Norway as a constitutional monarchy.
As required by the constitution, King Haakon will declare: "I promise and swear to rule the Kingdom of Norway in accordance with its constitution and laws, so help me God the Almighty and All-knowing."
His wife, Queen Mette-Marit, 53, who is recovering from a successful lung transplant in June, is due to be at his side, like Queen Sonja was in 1991 when Harald took the oath.
The new king's children, Crown Princess Ingrid Alexandra, 22, and Prince Sverre Magnus, 20, will also attend, as well as their grandmother, Sonja, 89.
Haakon automatically became king the moment his father passed away. There will be no coronation, as Norway abolished the practice in 1908.
After the ceremony, members of the public will be able to pay their respects before Harald's coffin, which is lying in state at the palace chapel until September 8. Large crowds are expected.
His funeral will take place in Oslo on September 9, with heads of state from around the world invited to attend.  — REUTERS
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Woman pleads guilty over RM17,300 baby transfer deal
Article:
SUNGAI PETANI: A 24-year-old woman pleaded guilty in the Sessions Court today to an alternative charge of taking part in a transaction intended to permanently transfer control of a baby in exchange for RM17,300 last month.
S. Kelsey entered the plea after the charge was read before Judge Nabisha Ibrahim.
The court fixed Oct 5 for remention and sentencing.
According to the charge, Kelsey took part in the transaction involving the baby, now 12 days old, at a private hospital between 7.30am on Aug 18 and 1.30am on Aug 21.
She was charged under Section 48(1) of the Child Act 2001, which carries a maximum fine of RM50,000, jail of up to 20 years, or both.
Earlier, defence counsel RSN Rayer sought a new date for the facts of the case and sentencing, as well as a lower bail amount, saying his client did not have a permanent job and had a family to support.
Rayer also asked the court to consider her condition, saying she was exhausted after being detained to assist investigations three days after giving birth last month.
The court granted bail of RM10,000 with one surety and ordered Kelsey to surrender her passport to the court and not interfere with prosecution witnesses.
In a separate case at the magistrate's court, Kelsey also pleaded guilty to possessing another person's identity card last month.
She was accused of possessing the identity card of a 33-year-old woman, knowing it belonged to someone else, at the same hospital at 1.30pm on Aug 21.
The offence under Regulation 25(1)(e) of the National Registration Regulations 1990 carries a maximum two-year jail term, a fine of up to RM3,000, or both.
Magistrate Muhammad Syaiful Akmal Mohamad Razi granted bail of RM1,500 with one surety and also fixed Oct 5 for mention and sentencing.

Title: Private helicopter deployed to search for 17 Malaysians missing in Nepal
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A private helicopter is being deployed today to search for 17 Malaysians who remain unaccounted for following flash floods in Nepal's Rasuwa district.
Fishtail Tours & Travels representative Roshan Panday said he had arranged for the helicopter to search for the group at their last known location.
"Today I am sending a helicopter privately. Let's see if we find any traces," he told the New Straits Times today.
Roshan said the helicopter was expected to depart within 2 hours, with the search expected to take between 45 and 60 minutes.
He confirmed that the helicopter would head towards the last known location of the 17 Malaysians, who were travelling together in the affected area.
"If it is possible, we are planning to land near the last spotted coordinates," he said.
However, he said poor weather and the high volume of SOS calls had hampered helicopter operations in the area.
"The weather is not so cooperative and also helicopter schedules are mostly hampered because of SOS calls," he said.
The latest search effort comes as efforts continue to locate the 17 Malaysians, who remain uncontactable following the flash floods in Rasuwa.
Roshan said the helicopter search would focus on finding any traces of the group, amid challenging weather conditions that have affected helicopter operations in the area.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nepal tragedy: Next of kin awaits call from authorities for DNA sample
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The next of kin of the victims who have still not been traced after the mudslide tragedy in Nepal a week ago are preparing to submit their deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) samples and are just waiting for a call from the authorities to do so.
Sivakumar Kalimuthu, 57, husband of victim Kalai Mathe Karuppaiah, 57, said his children are now on standby and waiting for official notification to carry out the identity profile cross-reference procedure.
He said that although his three children are in Singapore, Langkawi and Selangor, they have been given an explanation and understand the important need to provide the samples.
"The children are all ready, wait for tomorrow or whenever they call since yesterday and today are holidays. The children who are in Selangor can go and their DNA can be used, we are just waiting for a call from the police," he said when contacted by Bernama today.
Earlier, a closed-door briefing session by the Foreign Ministry on Sunday informed that the next of kin of Malaysians who have yet to be traced are encouraged to undergo DNA testing at the state police contingent headquarters.
The move is among the initial preparations following the discovery of several unidentified bodies in the disaster area, which had to be buried immediately due to the lack of suitable storage facilities at the location.
Commenting further, Sivakumar said his wife was among the Malaysian citizens who were reported to be still missing while following an expedition to Mount Kailash in Tibet, China, before losing contact due to the natural disaster.
Despite having to go through the DNA testing procedure, Sivakumar said he and his family still have high hopes and continue to pray that his wife is safe and can return home.
Wisma Putra informed that the number of Malaysians who have been reported to be uncontactable remains at 36 in China and 55 in Nepal following the devastating flash floods and landslides in the Rasuwa District, Nepal that occurred on August 26.
Anadolu Agency reported that the death toll from the devastating flash floods and landslides in Nepal and the Tibetan region of China has risen to 804, while nearly 3,300 are still missing.

Title: A family's four-day quest for a son lost in Nepal's floods ends
Article:
FOR four agonising days after floodwaters tore through Nepal's Rasuwa district, Ayush Khadka's family searched desperately for any sign that the 21-year-old civil servant was still alive.
The Khadkas were among thousands of families clinging to hope amid the chaos wrought by a glacial collapse that sent an unprecedented deluge of ice, rock, mud and debris crashing through valley towns and villages in Nepal and across the border in China.
Ayush had spoken to relatives the night before the flood, and his social media account even appeared to show him as online the following morning, a small sign that gave the family hope he had survived.
As reports of widespread destruction emerged on August 26, family members immediately began what would turn out to be a futile search.
For two days his paternal uncle, Ganesh Khadka, waited near the Nepali Army's Maithali Barrack in Nuwakot, one of the main coordination points for rescue and recovery efforts near the flood-ravaged region.
Despite repeatedly sharing Ayush's name, workplace and last known location in Timure with officials, the family received few answers, Ganesh said.
In a desperate attempt to learn more, relatives tried to reach Timure — the badly flood-hit town where Ayush had been stationed, hundreds of kilometres from the family home in Salyan district — but roads had been destroyed and all private helicopters had been requisitioned by the government for rescue operations.
Meanwhile, Ayush's maternal aunt, Laxmi Thapa, was searching for him about 200 km away in Chitwan, where bodies had been swept downstream by the flood and were being recovered.
Unknown to most family members at the time, authorities had already recovered a body believed to be Ayush's on the day of the disaster, which has killed at least 939 people and left about 4,000 missing.
On Aug 27, Laxmi visited a temporary holding centre where photographs of recovered bodies were being displayed on a television screen for identification by relatives.
One image immediately caught her attention. "I was about 70 per cent sure it was him," she said.
[[nid:1523548]]
She sent the photograph to other relatives, including Ganesh, for their opinions, but the family deliberately chose not to show it to Ayush's distressed mother, Muna Khadka.
The family scrutinised every visible detail: a mole on the left side of the chin appeared to match Ayush's, as did his beard.
They also recognised a black religious protection thread, known as a 'buti,' that he regularly wore on his left arm but had slipped towards his wrist.
Still, they remained unsure, and for days the search for Ayush continued.
Information arrived in fragments, often through unofficial channels. The distance between Salyan, Kathmandu, Nuwakot, Chitwan and the flood-ravaged border region complicated every effort to establish what had happened.
The uncertainty became even more painful as authorities prepared for the mass burial of unidentified bodies.
The Khadka family feared that victims from distant districts could be buried before relatives had enough time to reach Chitwan and identify them.
It was not until Aug 30, four days after the flood, that Ayush's mother was finally informed by the family that her son was dead.
The next morning, immediate and extended family members left Salyan at around 1 a.m. and travelled through the night to Chitwan. They arrived at around 8 am, exhausted after hours on the road but determined to obtain final confirmation.
There, standing before the recovered body, they confirmed what many had already feared.
Hours later, about 35 relatives gathered on the banks of the Narayani River to cremate a young man whose family had spent days searching for a different outcome.
"We were so happy when he was born, and equally happy when he passed the civil service examination at such a young age," Laxmi said.
"And now, he has left us in tears."

Title: Motorcyclist killed, another seriously hurt in four-vehicle crash [WATCH]
Article:
KEPALA BATAS: A motorcyclist was killed and another seriously injured in a four-vehicle crash on the North-South Expressway (Plus) here today.
Penang Fire and Rescue Department operations assistant director John Sagun Francis said the 1.04pm crash at Km127.4 involved 2 motorcycles and 2 Perodua Myvi cars.
"The operation involved rescuing a motorcyclist who had fallen down an embankment and bringing him to a safe location.

Title: DNA samples from family of missing Malaysian in Nepal floods to be taken tomorrow
Article:

The update was shared by K. Divya Varshini, 29, after she was informed by the relevant authorities.

Title: New coffee festival set to solidify Ipoh's identity as iconic 'Coffee City'
Article:
IPOH: The diverse coffee drinking culture of the country's multi-racial community, alongside elements of food, music, art and tourism, will enliven the Ipoh Coffee Vibes 2026 Festival which will be held for four days at the Riverfront Old Town Ipoh next to Jalan Sultan Iskandar here.
State Tourism, Industry, Investment and Corridor Development Committee chairman Loh Sze Yee said the festival, to be held for the first time, is targeting about 40,000 visitors and will take place from Sept 10 to 13.
He said 50 food and beverage stalls will participate in the festival while visitors will have the opportunity to enjoy coffee and watch performances along the Kinta River.
"Also, there will be an opportunity to get to know the story and uniqueness of Ipoh, thus strengthening efforts to make Ipoh a more iconic 'Coffee City' that has had its own identity since time immemorial," he said at a press conference on the festival here, today.
Loh said the Ipoh Coffee Vibes Festival 2026 would not only highlight white coffee but also bring together coffee cultures of various races and styles, including special coffees from the Malay community, Indian kopi tarik, international brands Starbucks as well as various snacks, desserts and foods themed with coffee or suitable for enjoying with coffee.
Loh said at the same time, participating coffee entrepreneurs would introduce 'Kopi Rakyat' specifically for the Ipoh Coffee Vibes Festival to allow the public to enjoy various types and flavours of coffee at more consumer-friendly prices.
He said various special performances combined with the coffee theme included a percussion performance themed to a white coffee shop, a kopi tarik performance, a coffee-themed flying roti canai performance and a flash mob performance of multicultural musical instruments.
"In addition, visitors will also enjoy free white coffee provided by Chang Jiang White Coffee
"Throughout the festival, visitors who spend RM50 and above at the event site are eligible to participate in a lucky draw to win cash vouchers that can be used immediately at the location while visitors who spend RM100 and above are eligible to redeem a set of Ipoh Coffee Vibes special edition souvenir collections," he said.

Title: EU frets over Kyiv's defences, 'hybrid' threat from Moscow
Article:
WICKLOW: EU defence and foreign ministers gathering in Ireland from Tuesday will grapple with bolstering Ukraine's air defences amid growing worries over Russia's campaign to destabilise Kyiv's European backers.
Moscow has taken advantage of Ukraine running low on US-built air defence missiles to pummel the country, while Kyiv has hit back against Russian infrastructure with its own long-range strikes.
"The Russian attacks on the Ukrainians are getting harsher and harsher," an EU official said, speaking on condition of anonymity.
Defence ministers – who meet Tuesday before foreign ministers hold talks Wednesday – are expected to speak with Ukraine's new acting defence minister Yevgeniy Khmara.
But there appears little they can do to massively increase the supply of desperately needed air interceptors to Ukraine – beyond pressuring European countries that still have stockpiles and urging the likes of Japan and South Korea to share more.
While the Kremlin escalates its air campaign against Ukraine, there have been growing worries that Moscow is also looking to deflect from its battlefield troubles by ramping up operations in Europe.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said his country has increasingly "found itself in the crosshairs of hybrid attackers" after an explosive-laden drone was found in August at Leizig airport, a crucial military transport hub.
Berlin hasn't yet officially blamed Russia over the incident – but the clear suggestion is that the finger of blame is pointing at Moscow.
Fuelling the concerns over Russia's intentions, CIA chief John Ratcliffe paid a surprise visit to Moscow last week, with US media reporting he warned Russia against attacking any Nato country.
EU officials insist that they don't see Moscow preparing for a military attack any time soon – but they are bracing for more incidents in the grey zone beneath open conflict.
"What we see is these hybrid and then not-so hybrid-attacks continuing and our assumption is that those will go on," the EU official said.
While Merz said that those behind the incidents in Germany will "pay for them", Europe has struggled to counter the low-level campaign of sabotage and interference it blames on Moscow.
Beyond ramping up intelligence sharing and police cooperation, the EU sees bolstering support for Ukraine and hitting Moscow with sanctions as ways to raise the costs for the Kremlin.
Brussels has floated fresh plans to add 1,600 more firms and individuals to its already long list of Russians sanctioned over the war.
Meanwhile discussion has resurfaced on whether the bloc should tap some 200 billion euros (US$235 billion) of frozen Russian central bank assets to fund Ukraine.
A proposal to use the funds failed last year after opposition from Belgium, where the bulk of the assets are held, and the EU came up with a 90-billion-euro loan for Kyiv off its own back.
But there is already a sense that money might not last the two years it was intended for and the EU may need to find a way sooner or later to use the immobilised Russian funds.
"As each day passes, the cost of the war is rising as Russia's relentless attacks continue unabated," the top diplomats of the Netherlands, Poland, Spain and Sweden wrote in a letter last week.
New British foreign minister Ed Miliband and Ukraine's Andriy Sybiga will join their EU counterparts, whose long-scheduled meeting is in Ireland as it holds the bloc's rotating presidency.
But while crises rage around the globe from Ukraine to Iran, the EU ministers will also open a debate on reforming how the bloc runs its diplomacy as it seeks impact in an increasingly hostile world.
While some are advocating to overhaul the EU's diplomatic service under foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas, others say now is not the time for institutional reshuffling and the 27 nations need to focus on better coordinating their positions.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Japan arrests man twice for hamster massacres
Article:
TOKYO: Police in Japan said Tuesday they had arrested a man over the killing of 30 hamsters at a hotel, weeks after he was detained for stomping to death 20 others.
The 36-year-old high school staffer in the northern region of Iwate teamed up with two different women at so-called "love hotels" – short-stay lodging meant for couples – where he allegedly killed hamsters in violation of animal protection laws, police told AFP.
The two women have also been arrested, said Hiroyuki Nasu, a senior police official in the city of Miyako, Iwate.
The main suspect's arrest on Monday was for his "gratuitous killings" in late March of about 30 hamsters, carried out in collusion with a 20-year-old woman, Nasu told AFP.
The suspect's smartphone confiscated by police contained videos of the killings, as well as text messages with the woman that showed them plotting the act.
"Where are we going to kill the hamsters and have fun?" Nasu quoted one of the exchanged messages as saying.
The suspect was first detained in July for the separate killing in February of around 20 hamsters with a 19-year-old woman.
Police will continue to investigate the suspect and examine whether he may have committed other similar acts, the police official said.

Title: Saifuddin Nasution expresses appreciation to marine police on its 79th anniversary
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail expressed his appreciation to the marine police force in conjunction with its 79th anniversary celebration today.
He said that since its establishment 79 years ago, the force has stood firm in safeguarding the country's waters, defending the nation's sovereignty and protecting the people's interests.
"Behind every patrol and operation lies the bravery, discipline and sacrifice of our marine police personnel, who are always prepared to face any challenges to ensure the country's waters remain peaceful and protected.
"My highest appreciation and deepest gratitude to all personnel, including those who served with the team before," he said in a Facebook post today.
He also hopes the marine police will continue to progress, be efficient and credible in defending national security.

Title: Home Ministry developing framework for CCFC establishment next year
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Home Ministry, through the Institute of Public Security of Malaysia (IPSOM), is developing a comprehensive governance and operational framework for the establishment of the Cyber Crime Fusion Centre (CCFC), which is expected to be operational next year.
IPSOM deputy chief executive SAC Dr Shazrin Azlin Ruslan said the initiative was a continuation of the National Cybercrime Threat Action Plan study undertaken by IPSOM in collaboration with Cyber Security Academia Malaysia (CSAM) and local universities last year.
She said the local universities involved in the study were Universiti Sains Islam Malaysia (USIM), Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia (UKM), Universiti Putra Malaysia (UPM) and Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM).
"As a continuation of the previous research, this year we are conducting a study on the establishment of the CCFC, focusing on the development of its governance and operational models," she said when appearing as a guest on Bernama Radio's Fokus 30 programme today.
Shazrin Azlin said the development of the centre would also be discussed extensively at the 6th International Cyber Resilience Conference (CRC) 2026, which brings together cybersecurity experts from 43 countries in Bangi, Selangor, from today.
She said the study on the establishment of the CCFC had identified 47 types of cyber-enabled crimes and 10 types of cyber-dependent crimes from the Home Ministry's perspective.
She said cyber-enabled crimes were not limited to fraud and scams, but also encompassed various conventional crimes that had shifted to online and digital platforms.
Meanwhile, CRC 2026 general chairman Prof Dr Ainuddin Wahid Abdul Wahab said the conference served not only as a platform for information-sharing, but also as a forum to formulate strategic approaches to address increasingly complex and cross-border digital threats.
"CRC 2026 is not just an academic conference, but also a platform for us to turn knowledge into action," he said.
He said 163 working papers that had undergone a thorough screening process would be presented at the three-day conference, which would be launched by Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail tomorrow.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Cross-Border Insolvency Act enhances legal certainty, safeguards creditors and stakeholders
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The enforcement of the Cross-Border Insolvency Act 2026 (Act 877), which came into force on Aug 28, will enhance the efficiency of cross-border insolvency case management.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said and Minister of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali said the Act also improves legal certainty and protects the interests of creditors and stakeholders.
"Act 877 provides a dedicated mechanism for handling insolvency proceedings involving debtors, assets, creditors, or proceedings in more than one jurisdiction.
"This Act is the result of collaboration between Azalina and Armizan, in line with the Madani Government's legal reform agenda to ensure that the country's legal framework remains relevant, progressive, and aligned with economic, social and international trade developments," the ministers said in a joint statement today.
The statement further noted that Act 877 is based on the Model Law on Cross-Border Insolvency adopted by the United Nations Commission on International Trade Law (UNCITRAL).
"This Model has been adapted to align with Malaysia's laws, judicial practices, economic conditions, and public interests, to ensure that its implementation takes into account the nation's needs and interests," the statement read.
The statement further noted that enforcement of Act 877 will help maximise the value of debtors' assets and facilitate business rescue efforts.
"These measures are crucial for protecting investments and preserving jobs, particularly in situations involving insolvency proceedings across more than one jurisdiction," the statement added.
The clearer framework for handling such proceedings will strengthen coordination and cooperation between courts and relevant authorities.
The statement added that the Madani Government is committed to ensuring that Act 877 is implemented in an orderly, efficient and effective manner to bolster the nation's economic resilience.
The implementation of the Act is also expected to support Malaysia's position as an international trade and investment destination with a relevant and progressive legal framework.
