Title: Duta Enclave: Court told RM1.39mil govt payout to Semantan Estate more than adequate
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court was told today that the RM1.39 million in compensation paid by the Government of Malaysia to Semantan Estate (1952) Sdn Bhd for the acquisition of 263.272 acres (106.544ha) of land, known as the Duta Enclave, in 1956 was more than adequate.
Finance Ministry Valuation and Property Services Department assistant director Tan Tat Khuan, 40, stated that his analysis found the sixth comparable property, Lot 1348, Mukim Kuala Lumpur, to be the most suitable benchmark, as it shared similar characteristics, namely being freehold agricultural land.
"I have prepared an expert valuation report to determine adequate compensation, in accordance with the Court of Appeal Order dated June 24, 2025, which, among others, fixed the valuation date for determining compensation for the said land as Dec 3, 1956.
"After adjusting for factors such as time, location, stratum, accessibility, development potential, size, shape and topography, the adjusted rate for the sixth comparable property was $3,320 per acre (0.4ha).
"Taking into account the land area of 263.272 acres, the total market value determined was $875,000, equivalent to RM875,000," he said in his witness statement during the Duta Enclave compensation assessment hearing before Judge Roslan Mat Nor.
The "$" symbol in the valuation denotes the Malayan dollar, which was the legal tender in 1956 and stood at par with the Malaysian ringgit.
Tan clarified that should the court adopt the total freehold area of 700.75 acres (283.58ha) as the basis for valuation, adjusted proportionately to the acquired land area of 263.272 acres (106.54ha), the compensation he recommended under Valuation Basis 1 would amount to $875,000, equivalent to RM875,000.
"Given that the government had previously paid compensation of $1,390,602.70 (in 1956) to the plaintiff (Semantan Estate), that amount exceeds the compensation I recommended under Valuation Basis 1.
"Therefore, in my view, the compensation already paid to the plaintiff was more than adequate, and no additional compensation ought to be considered by the court," he said.
He said that upon reviewing the report prepared by the plaintiff's expert witness, Foo Gee Jen, who acted as valuer for Semantan Estate, he found that all the comparables relied upon pertained to small bungalow plots, whereas the subject land constituted a sizeable agricultural parcel with residential development potential.
He said three of the comparables involved transactions post-dating the valuation date and could not be considered, in accordance with Paragraph 1C of the First Schedule to the Land Acquisition Act 1960.
He also observed that the plaintiff's expert had failed to account for factors such as accessibility, land use and the increase in value of the remaining land resulting from the acquisition.
Tan further submitted that the claims for severance and injurious affection advanced by the plaintiff's expert were also unfounded, irrelevant, unsustainable and ought not to be considered by the court.
"Based on my assessment, the report prepared by the plaintiff's expert is unreasonable and lacks a solid basis to be relied upon by the court. As such, I recommend that the court reject the said valuation report," he said.
The hearing continues on Oct 16.
On Nov 13, 2025, the Federal Court dismissed Semantan Estate's application for leave to appeal against the Court of Appeal's decision that the Registrar of Titles of the Federal Territory was not required to register the 263.272acre (106.54ha) land in the Duta Enclave in the company's name.
Accordingly, the Court of Appeal's decision in favour of the government stands and the case was subsequently remitted to the High Court for hearing on the assessment of damages.
On June 24, 2025, the Court of Appeal ruled that Semantan Estate was not entitled to ownership of the said land, but the company was entitled to adequate compensation based on the value of the land in 1956, when it was acquired by the government.
The land, situated at the prime location of Jalan Duta, currently houses, among others, the Inland Revenue Board complex, several government buildings, the National Hockey Stadium, Institute of Islamic Understanding Malaysia and Federal Territory Mosque.
In 2003, Semantan Estate filed a suit against the government, alleging trespass arising from the unlawful acquisition of the land from the company.
In 2009, Judicial Commissioner Zura Yahya ruled that Semantan Estate retained its beneficial interest in the 263.27-acre land, and that it had been unlawfully acquired and trespassed upon by the government.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 3-year-old boy dies after falling through gap on Victoria Bridge
Article:
SUNGAI SIPUT: A 3-year-old boy died after falling five metres from Victoria Bridge in Enggor here yesterday.
The victim was pronounced dead at 7.40pm at Kuala Kangsar Hospital following the incident, which occurred at 6pm.
District police chief Superintendent Charan Ai Wan said the victim was walking on the historical bridge with his 42-year-old father when the incident happened.
"The victim was holding hands with his father while walking on the bridge before falling five metres through a gap in the structure.
"After falling onto the paved road below, the victim, who was still alive at the time, was rushed to the hospital emergency ward but was pronounced dead at 7.40pm," he said when contacted today.
He said the victim, from Kluang, Johor, was visiting Victoria Bridge on a family holiday.
A survey at the scene today found the iconic bridge closed to visitors for safety reasons, with police and the Kuala Kangsar Municipal Council cordoning off the area with caution tape.
A stallholder near the location, who wanted to be known only as Nyah, said her husband and son-in-law were manning their stall when they heard a loud thud, initially mistaking it for a dropped bag before realising a child had fallen.
"Since yesterday was a public holiday for National Day, there were many visitors, including those with young children, taking photos at Victoria Bridge," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Air Itam clash involved rival factions of 04 gang, police confirm
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Police have confirmed that the recent violent clash in Air Itam involved members of the 04 gang operating independently under separate factions.
State police chief Datuk Dennis Lim said the 04 name was being used by distinct groups operating in different areas for their own interests.
"It is a clash involving different factions of the 04 gang," he told reporters at the state police headquarters here today.
Lim was commenting on the
clash
, which occurred at 2.45am on Aug 29 in front of SJK(C) Kong Min involving two men aged 17 and 25.
Lim said the incident stemmed from a debt dispute, with one group attempting to collect money owed on behalf of another party.
"This was not related to illegal moneylending. They were helping to collect a debt, but the matter escalated into a dispute and a fight," he said.
The confrontation worsened when one suspect allegedly attempted to ram members of the opposing group with a vehicle before weapons were used.
Lim clarified that two men who were severely injured in separate attacks were not gang members, but victims of mistaken identity.
"They were victims. They happened to be wearing similar-coloured clothing, and the suspects mistakenly thought they were members of the other group," he said.
The two victims were returning from a Hungry Ghost Festival event when they were attacked, he added.
Lim said both victims sustained serious injuries and were reported to be in stable condition.
Police have detained 13 men, including three minors, to assist in investigations.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tanjung Bungah dog attack: MBPP cancels licence, issues RM250 compound
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: The Penang Island City Council (MBPP) has cancelled a dog licence and issued its owner a RM250 compound following an attack on a stray dog in Tanjung Bungah.
Mayor Datuk A. Rajendran said the action was taken under the Muncipal Council of Penang Island Dogs Bylaws following the incident, which went viral on social media.
He said the dog had not been released to its owner, who had been advised to lodge a police report.
"The owner informed authorities that another person had taken the dog out for a walk on the day of the incident," he told the NST.
The incident in Tanjung Bungah sparked public concern after footage of the
dog attacking a stray
was widely circulated on social media.
The Department of Veterinary Services (DVS) is leading investigations into the incident, while the city council had earlier captured the dog involved in the attack.
Earlier today, DVS urged the public to lodge a
police report
to enable an investigation into the viral incident.
It said those with allegations or evidence that a person had encouraged or provoked an animal to attack should lodge a report.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: UNHCR warns Myanmar remains unsafe for refugees to return
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The United Nations refugee agency said on Tuesday it was not involved in Malaysia's planned repatriation of Myanmar refugees, and warned that it remains unsafe for them to return to the war-torn country.
The Home Ministry said last week it had finalised the first phase of a voluntary repatriation programme that will see 1,476 refugees returned to Myanmar on September 29.
Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim had earlier said Myanmar had agreed to repatriate 5,000 Rohingya, amid rising tensions over the refugees within local communities in Malaysia.
The UNHCR said an ongoing armed conflict and violence across Myanmar meant there could not be a safe, dignified and sustainable voluntary return of refugees.
"Under customary international law – a binding obligation on all states – no one should be sent to a country where their rights or freedoms may be at risk. Any refugee return must be voluntary, based on an informed decision, and take place in conditions of safety and dignity," it said in an emailed statement to Reuters.
"UNHCR urges that careful consideration be given to the protection needs of all those concerned before they are returned to Myanmar, and stands ready to engage with relevant authorities on protection safeguards."
A Home Ministry spokesperson declined to comment on the UNHCR statement, referring to its earlier remarks that the repatriation process was voluntary.
Thousands of refugees have fled Myanmar since a 2021 military coup that sparked a nationwide civil war.
As of February, Malaysia had around 193,800 refugees from Myanmar of various ethnicities, including Rohingya and Chin, according to UNHCR data. Activists, however, say many more remain unregistered.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: RM1bil additional micro-financing should come with faster approval: FMM
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The additional RM1 billion in micro-financing facilities, which brings the total allocation for 2026 to RM6 billion from RM5 billion, should be accompanied by simple application procedures, affordable financing terms, and faster approval and disbursement, said the Federation of Malaysian Manufacturing (FMM).
FMM president Jacob Lee Chor Kok said the move was important as small and medium enterprises (SMEs) continue to face pressure from rising operating costs and cash flow constraints.
"The government should also ensure adequate access to financing for eligible small manufacturers and manufacturing-related businesses.
"These measures can help free up resources for businesses to sustain operations, retain workers and undertake productivity-enhancing investments," he said in a statement today.
Prime minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced six immediate measures aimed at easing cost pressures on businesses and households ahead of Budget 2027 during his National Day 2026 address on Aug 30.
Lee also said that FMM recognises the government's decision to introduce measures that can provide more immediate support as businesses continue to contend with operating cost pressures, cash-flow constraints and an increasingly challenging and competitive business environment.
"While several of the initiatives are primarily targeted at households and the wider community, they will also have positive spillover effects on businesses and the economy," he added.
The federation also welcomes the decision to increase the annual sales threshold for mandatory e-Invoicing to RM3 million from RM1 million under the higher e-Invoicing exemption threshold as this will provide meaningful relief to smaller businesses by reducing compliance costs, administrative requirements and the resources needed to implement and maintain e-Invoicing systems.
"For businesses with annual sales between RM1 million and RM3 million that have already implemented e-Invoicing under the previous threshold, FMM calls on the Inland Revenue Board of Malaysia to provide early clarification on whether they may opt out following the revised threshold or continue participating voluntarily," he added.
Lee emphasised that businesses that have already invested in systems and commenced implementation should continue to receive appropriate technical guidance and support as early adopters.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: ‘Literally tasting the smoke’: Sarawakians suffer as haze worsens
Article:
KUCHING, September 1 — Air quality in Malaysia's Sarawak state deteriorated further today as smoke from Indonesian forest fires drove up respiratory complaints and sent residents scrambling for protective masks.
Six districts in Sarawak, on Borneo, recorded hazardous Air Pollutant Index (API) readings, including the state capital, Kuching, where the API hit 407.
Under national guidelines, levels above 300 are classed as hazardous, while readings beyond 500 could prompt consideration of a local emergency.
Schools in Kuching shut two weeks ago, and the state has seen supplies of haze-rated masks dwindle.
Resident Ivana Mason, 37, said five pharmacies she visited had sold out of respirators designed to filter fine particles.
“The only ones available were standard medical masks, which aren't effective at protecting against fine haze particles,” she told AFP.
Mason said the worsening air had also affected her health, causing a sore throat and aggravating her asthma.
“I've been sneezing non-stop, and my eyes are constantly watery,” she said, adding that the haze had forced her to stop going to her usual non-air-conditioned gym and limit trips outside.
“If I do, I can literally taste the smoke in my mouth.”
Local pharmacist Dawi Bakri, 31, said demand for masks had risen significantly since the haze worsened, making it difficult to maintain sufficient stocks.
“All types of masks have been selling faster than usual,” he said.
Md Khairulanwar Asri, 33, an occupational therapist at Sarawak Heart Centre, warned that poor air could hit people with existing heart or respiratory conditions, as well as elderly patients with multiple ailments.
“People exposed to poor air quality could experience coughing, throat and eye irritation, and shortness of breath.
“These symptoms can also affect a person's endurance and ability to comfortably carry out daily activities, particularly activities that require physical exertion,” Khairulanwar said.
Sarawak has been among the worst-affected areas in the latest haze episode, as smoke from Indonesian forest and land fires drifts across the border.
Malaysia's health ministry has reported rising cases of asthma and conjunctivitis nationwide as air quality worsens.
Sarawak authorities said cloud-seeding operations could begin as early as Thursday if the weather allows. — AFP

Title: Former Tabung Haji chairman, ex-Treasury sec-gen released from MACC custody in RCI-linked probe
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 1 — A former Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) chairman and a former Treasury secretary-general were reportedly released from Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) custody today in an investigation linked to a royal commission of inquiry (RCI) report on the pilgrims’ fund.
Harian Metro
reported that the two men were released this morning after being remanded on August 27.
A source reportedly said investigators had completed recording statements from the two men, who are in their 60s and carry the honorifics “Datuk Seri” and “Tan Sri”.
The politician and former TH chairman and the former Finance Ministry official were arrested at the MACC headquarters in Putrajaya on August 26.
The case is being investigated under Section 23 of the MACC Act 2009 for using one’s office or position to solicit gratification.
A former TH chief executive officer was previously detained and remanded in connection with the same investigation.
Before that, MACC detained seven people comprising a shipping company chief executive officer, two company directors and four former members of TH’s senior management.
The cases involved separate allegations concerning documents containing false information, a proposed investment in a construction company and a hotel lease in Saudi Arabia.
The 252-page RCI report, which examined TH’s management and operations from 2014 to 2020, was declassified and released on July 29, four years after it was completed.
Among its recommendations were amendments to the Tabung Haji Act 1995 to bar active politicians from serving as directors of TH and its subsidiaries, as well as expertise requirements for board members.

Title: Three-year-old boy found dead below Victoria Bridge in Kuala Kangsar
Article:
KUALA KANGSAR, Sept 1 — A three-year-old boy was reportedly found dead on a road beneath the Victoria Bridge in Enggor here yesterday evening.
Sinar Harian
reported that Abdul Rafee Abdul Halim was taken to Kuala Kangsar Hospital, where he was pronounced dead at about 7.40pm.
Sungai Siput district police chief Supt Charan Ai Wan said the boy had been walking across the bridge while holding his father’s hand before he was found about five metres below it at around 6.30pm.
“After the incident, the victim’s mother, who was at the scene, saw her son on the road beneath the bridge,” he was quoted as saying.
The youngest of five siblings, Abdul Rafee had travelled with his family from Kluang, Johor, for a holiday in Kuala Kangsar and was visiting the bridge when the incident occurred.
The Kuala Kangsar Municipal Council subsequently cordoned off the bridge with safety tape.

Title: Ayer Itam brawl involved Geng 04 members in debt dispute, Penang police say
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Sept 1 — Police have confirmed that an armed fight that caused two individuals to suffer severe injuries in front of a National Type Chinese Primary School in Ayer Itam here on Saturday involved Geng 04 members.
Penang police chief Datuk Dennis Lim Kwang Keng said all 13 men arrested to facilitate investigations into the case are believed to be members of the same gang but in different areas and the fight was due to a misunderstanding over debts.
“Investigations found that the debt did not involve unlicensed money lending or loansharking but they were trying to help a certain party to retrieve the debt from members of their gang.
“They started out discussing the issue properly but failed to reach an agreement before a dispute and the fight occurred till a suspect tried to ram several individuals there with a vehicle,” he told reporters at the Penang contingent police headquarters here today.
He said the two severely injured men, in their 30s, were not gang members but were attacked when they were misidentified as suspects involved in the fight, adding the victims were on their way back from a religious festival when they were attacked by the group.
“They are victims who coincidentally were wearing clothes with similar colours and were assumed to be members involved in the fight, both of them suffered severe injuries but are now in stable condition and being treated in the hospital,” he said, adding that the case is being investigated under Section 326 and 148 of the Penal Code. — Bernama

Title: Penang police arrest married couple, two others in drug syndicate on Thai intel tip
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Sept 1 — Police have arrested four members of an international drug syndicate, including a married couple, and seized 86 kilogrammes of methamphetamine worth RM4.31 million in a series of raids in Selangor and Penang recently.
Penang police chief Datuk Dennis Lim Kwang Keng said the success was the result of intelligence sharing between the Royal Malaysia Police and the Royal Thai Police after Thai authorities arrested a Malaysian man in Hua Hin, Thailand, on Aug 8.
He said the Malaysian suspect was arrested at a roadblock after 166 kg of methamphetamine was found hidden in his car.
Thai narcotics police conducted an investigation and obtained intelligence, which was subsequently shared with the Malaysian Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID).
“Acting on the intelligence, we launched Op Zorav Terra to cripple the syndicate. During the operation in Selangor on Aug 13, police arrested two local men and a Thai woman who is the wife of one of them, who acted as the syndicate’s transporters,” he told a press conference at the Penang police contingent headquarters here today.
Lim said that in a follow-up operation on Aug 14, a Bukit Aman NCID team arrested a 19-year-old man in Butterworth before inspecting a Nissan Teana parked in a hotel car park there.
The team found 80 packages containing 86 kg of methamphetamine worth RM4.31 million in a specially constructed compartment in the vehicle’s boot.
He said the first three suspects are believed to have brought in the drugs from Thailand using the car.
Investigations found that the three suspects had allegedly made several trips transporting drugs into Malaysia.
“The syndicate smuggled drugs into Malaysia using Malaysian-registered vehicles that had been modified. The drugs were intended for the local market and possibly to be transported to other countries, with the syndicate using Malaysia as a transit country,” he said.
He said the syndicate was believed to have been active since June last year, with each delivery earning the suspects about RM6,000 for acting as transporters.
According to him, the syndicate’s mastermind was based in Thailand, while its members and network were also operating in Malaysia.
He said efforts to track down those involved are being intensified by the authorities in both Malaysia and Thailand.
Lim said the NCID also seized five vehicles of various types, estimated to be worth RM420,700, under the Dangerous Drugs (Forfeiture of Property) Act 1988.
“All the suspects, aged between 19 and 25, have no previous records. However, urine screening found that one suspect tested positive for ketamine. The case is being investigated under Section 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952,” he said.
Also present at the press conference were Bukit Aman NCID deputy director (Enforcement/Prevention/General Policing) Datuk Zairulnizam Mohd Zainuddin @ Hilmi and Royal Thai Police Narcotics Suppression Bureau Intelligence Sub-Division Police Colonel Sintu Chanpaibooi. — Bernama

Title: Duta Enclave: Court told RM1.39m payout to Semantan Estate was more than adequate
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, September 1 — The High Court was told today that the RM1.39 million in compensation paid by the Government of Malaysia to Semantan Estate (1952) Sdn Bhd for the acquisition of 263.272 acres of land, known as the Duta Enclave, in 1956 was more than adequate.
Ministry of Finance, Valuation and Property Services Department assistant director Tan Tat Khuan, 40, stated that his analysis found the sixth comparable property, Lot 1348, Mukim Kuala Lumpur, to be the most suitable benchmark, as it shared similar characteristics, namely being freehold agricultural land.
“I have prepared an expert valuation report to determine adequate compensation, in accordance with the Court of Appeal Order dated June 24, 2025, which, among others, fixed the valuation date for determining compensation for the said land as December 3, 1956.
“After adjusting for factors such as time, location, stratum, accessibility, development potential, size, shape and topography, the adjusted rate for the sixth comparable property was $3,320 per acre.
“Taking into account the land area of 263.272 acres, the total market value determined was $875,000, equivalent to RM875,000,” he said in his witness statement during the Duta Enclave compensation assessment hearing before Judge Roslan Mat Nor.
The “$” symbol in the valuation denotes the Malayan dollar, which was the legal tender in 1956 and stood at par with the Malaysian ringgit.
Tan clarified that should the court adopt the total freehold area of 700.75 acres as the basis for valuation, adjusted proportionately to the acquired land area of 263.272 acres, the compensation he recommended under Valuation Basis 1 would amount to $875,000, equivalent to RM875,000.
“Given that the government had previously paid compensation of $1,390,602.70 (in 1956) to the plaintiff (Semantan Estate), that amount exceeds the compensation I recommended under Valuation Basis 1.
“Therefore, in my view, the compensation already paid to the plaintiff was more than adequate, and no additional compensation ought to be considered by the court,” he said.
Tan said that upon reviewing the report prepared by the plaintiff’s expert witness, Foo Gee Jen, who acted as valuer for Semantan Estate, he found that all the comparables relied upon pertained to small bungalow plots, whereas the subject land constituted a sizeable agricultural parcel with residential development potential.
He added that three of the comparables involved transactions post-dating the valuation date and could not be considered, in accordance with Paragraph 1C of the First Schedule to the Land Acquisition Act 1960.
He also observed that the plaintiff’s expert had failed to account for factors such as accessibility, land use and the increase in value of the remaining land resulting from the acquisition.
Tan further submitted that the claims for severance and injurious affection advanced by the plaintiff’s expert were also unfounded, irrelevant, unsustainable and ought not to be considered by the court.
“Based on my assessment, the report prepared by the plaintiff’s expert is unreasonable and lacks a solid basis to be relied upon by the court. As such, I recommend that the court reject the said valuation report,” he said.
The hearing continues on October 16.
On November 13, 2025, the Federal Court dismissed Semantan Estate’s application for leave to appeal against the Court of Appeal’s decision that the Registrar of Titles of the Federal Territory was not required to register the 263.272-acre land in the Duta Enclave in the company’s name.
Accordingly, the Court of Appeal’s decision in favour of the government stands and the case was subsequently remitted to the High Court for hearing on the assessment of damages.
On June 24, 2025, the Court of Appeal ruled that Semantan Estate was not entitled to ownership of the said land, but the company was entitled to adequate compensation based on the value of the land in 1956, when it was acquired by the government.
The land, situated at the prime location of Jalan Duta, currently houses, among others, the Inland Revenue Board complex, several government buildings, the National Hockey Stadium, Institute of Islamic Understanding Malaysia and Federal Territory Mosque.
In 2003, Semantan Estate filed a suit against the government, alleging trespass arising from the unlawful acquisition of the land from the company.
In 2009, Judicial Commissioner Zura Yahya ruled that Semantan Estate retained its beneficial interest in the 263.27-acre land, and that it had been unlawfully acquired and trespassed upon by the government. — Bernama

Title: Former PM Muhyiddin, ‘Azman’ and ‘Adam’ listed in same July 2020 golf game at Tropicana, witness tells court
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 1 — Former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin played in a golf game in July 2020 at Tropicana Golf Club with 14 other players, including two individuals identified as “Azman” and “Adam”, Tropicana Golf & Country Resort Berhad (TGCRB) employee Saravanan Subaramaniam told the High Court today.
TGCRB group head of security Saravanan said this while testifying as the 28th prosecution witness in Muhyiddin’s power abuse and money laundering trial.
Saravanan said Tropicana Golf Club’s digital golf registration system showed that Muhyiddin and the 14 other individuals had played there in four “flights”, or groups, on July 19, 2020, with a single invoice issued for all 15 players.
The invoice was recorded under four players’ names, including Muhyiddin’s name.
Based on documents known as Green Fees Tags, which were printed from the golf club’s computer system, Saravanan confirmed Muhyiddin had played with three other players in the first flight with a tee-off time of 8.49am, while “Azman” and three others were in the second flight, teeing off at 8.57am, and “Adam” and three others were in the fourth flight, which teed off at 9.13am.
Saravanan did not provide the full names of the golf players “Azman” and “Adam” and was not asked to confirm if they referred to any individuals who had previously testified or been mentioned in this trial.
Last week, Bumiputera Contractors Association of Malaysia (PKBM) president Datuk Seri Azman Yusoff, testifying as the 27th prosecution witness, said he had played at the Tan Sri Muhyiddin Charity Golf (TSMCG) tournament at Tropicana Golf Club in July 2020.
Azman had said that he, Muhyiddin and “Adam” had played in three separate teams in the same game and that he had a one-on-one meeting with Muhyiddin at 3pm after the tournament.
Azman had testified that Muhyiddin had, in that meeting, spontaneously said contractors could donate directly to the latter’s political party, Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia, and that the spontaneous remark was made during a conversation about government projects for Bumiputera contractors.
Azman last week also testified that he and his company KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd had donated RM4.8 million to Bersatu after getting a RM62 million government project under the Muhyiddin administration’s Jana Wibawa programme due to Muhyiddin’s July 2020 remarks.
Tropicana Golf & Country Resort group head of security S. Saravanan arrives at the Kuala Lumpur Court Complex to testify in former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin’s trial, September 1, 2026. — Picture by Sayuti Zainudin
Golf club’s computer records on July 2020 players not modified, witness says
Today, Saravanan explained that a person would have to book a game at Tropicana Golf Club by entering the names of all the players, as well as the date and time, into the club’s computerised registration system.
Saravanan said he did not know who had booked the July 19, 2020 game without referring to the club’s system, adding that the information provided was considered accurate unless changes were requested by the person who booked it.
Saravanan said any such changes by the person who booked the game must be made before tee-off and before the invoice is issued, and no changes can be made in the computer system once the invoice and Green Fees Tags have been issued.
Based on the club’s data in its computer system, Saravanan told deputy public prosecutor Wan Nur Iman Wan Ahmad Afzal that no changes had been made by the person who booked the July 19, 2020 game.
Earlier, under cross-examination by Muhyiddin’s lawyer Chetan Jethwani, Saravanan agreed that the golf club’s staff only key in the names of golfers provided by the person who booked the game without checking the names.
Saravanan agreed that the accuracy of the information provided could be verified by the person who made the booking.
While golf players are usually required to pay for the game and have invoices issued before the game starts, Saravanan said there are “special cases” involving VIP guests where the club would respect them by not asking them to pay first.
“In our case, at that time YAB Tan Sri was the prime minister, so we don't want to rush to issue invoice,” he told deputy public prosecutor Khairunnissa Hazwani Omar, referring to Muhyiddin, who was the PM then.
Saravanan also highlighted that the July 19, 2020 golf game involving Muhyiddin was “complimentary”, with no payment required as it was borne by the golf club’s management.
Chetan had earlier today questioned why the invoice could be issued hours after the July 19, 2020 game started, with Saravanan saying that this was possible when no payment was needed.
Was the July 2020 game a tournament or friendly game?
Asked by deputy public prosecutor Khairunnissa Hazwani Omar, Saravanan said that the July 19, 2020 game could refer to either a normal golf game or a tournament.
“Usually if playing in a small group among themselves, we call it a ‘friendly game’ among themselves.
“If it is a tournament and contest, it refers to a big group, usually over 10 to 20 flight, namely with total players of around 40 to 160,” Saravanan replied.
Last week, Muhyiddin’s lawyer Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad had sought to challenge Azman’s testimony that he had joined the TSMCG tournament in July 2020 in the morning before his solo meeting with Muhyiddin in the afternoon.
Amer had said that the golf tournament only took place in October 2020 in Desaru, Johor, and not in July 2020, but Azman replied that he was unsure and could not remember before confirming that there was such a tournament in October 2020.
Azman ultimately disagreed with Amer’s suggestion last week that the July 2020 golf game he joined was not a TSMCG tournament.
Today, deputy public prosecutor Noralis Mat informed the High Court that the prosecution would not be calling Adam Radlan Adam Muhammad to testify as a witness in this trial but may offer him as a witness to the defence.
Previously, businessman Lian Tan Chuan told this trial that Azman had introduced him to Adam Radlan as Muhyiddin’s close friend and that Azman had said Adam Radlan frequently played golf with Muhyiddin.
Lian previously said he had handed over letters of interest in a Jana Wibawa project tender from five companies, including his Bumiputera firm Nepturis Sdn Bhd, to Adam Radlan to be passed to Muhyiddin and that Nepturis had given RM1 million to Bersatu after getting the RM141 million project.
In this trial, Muhyiddin is facing seven charges, namely four counts of alleged power abuse to obtain RM225.3 million in bribes for his party, Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (from Nepturis Sdn Bhd, Datuk Seri Azman Yusoff, KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd, Bukhary Equity Sdn Bhd and Mamfor Sdn Bhd), and three counts of alleged money laundering involving money that Bersatu received from Bukhary Equity.
The trial before High Court judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin is scheduled to resume tomorrow.
